title: Extension System & Capability Discovery
description:
Implement a Feature Collection Pattern (similar to ASP.NET Core HttpContext.Features) to solve feature fragmentation across providers. Enables type-safe capability discovery without polluting core interfaces.

## Goals
1. Discover which features a generic client instance supports
2. Access specialized features in a type-safe manner
3. Avoid polluting core interfaces (IChatCompletionClient, IEmbeddingClient) with provider-specific methods

## Architecture
- IFeatureCollection container with Get<T>/Set<T>
- IHasFeatures marker interface on all client interfaces
- Provider-specific feature interfaces (e.g. IImageEmbeddingFeature)

## Phases
- Phase 1: Core Infrastructure (IFeatureCollection, IHasFeatures, update interfaces)
- Phase 2: Feature Definitions (IImageEmbeddingFeature, future IToolCallingFeature, IJsonModeFeature)
- Phase 3: Provider Implementation (Cohere, Azure AI Inference image embeddings)

### 1. Add ContentParts parameter to the LlmMessage record

Current signature:
```csharp
public sealed record LlmMessage(
    LlmRole Role,
    string Content,
    string? ToolCallId = null,
    IReadOnlyList<ToolCall>? ToolCalls = null);
```

New signature (add one optional parameter at the end):
```csharp
public sealed record LlmMessage(
    LlmRole Role,
    string Content,
    string? ToolCallId = null,
    IReadOnlyList<ToolCall>? ToolCalls = null,
    /// <summary>
    /// Multimodal content parts. When non-null, providers use this instead of <see cref="Content"/>
    /// for building the request. Text-only callers continue using <see cref="Content"/> as before.
    /// </summary>
    IReadOnlyList<MessageContentPart>? ContentParts = null);
```

```csharp
public static LlmMessage WithImage(string text, string imagePath) =>
    new(LlmRole.User, string.Empty, ContentParts: new MessageContentPart[]
    {
        new TextContentPart(text),
        new ImageFileContentPart(imagePath)
    });

public static LlmMessage WithBase64Image(string text, string base64Data, string mediaType) =>
    new(LlmRole.User, string.Empty, ContentParts: new MessageContentPart[]
    {
        new TextContentPart(text),
        new ImageBase64ContentPart(base64Data, mediaType)
    });
```

- All existing code using `new LlmMessage(LlmRole.User, "hello")` continues to work unchanged.

title: Strengthen Azure AI Inference tool-calling integration tests
description:
## Problem

The Azure AI Inference tool-calling integration tests (`AzureAiInferenceToolCallingIntegrationTests.cs`) convert provider errors for unsupported models into warnings and return early. This means the test suite can produce an all-green result even when tool calling is effectively never verified for any configured model.

This is a false-positive risk: if all configured models happen to not support tool calling, the tests pass with only warnings, giving the impression that tool calling is working when it was never actually tested.

## Current Behavior

```csharp
// Pseudocode of current pattern:
if (!response.IsSuccess)
{
    TestContext.WriteLine($"Warning: {model} does not support tool calling");
    return; // test passes without any assertion
}
```

## Desired Behavior

1. **At least one model must pass strict assertions** — Track across the parameterized test cases whether at least one model successfully completed tool calling. If no model succeeds, the test suite should fail or produce an inconclusive result.
2. **Unsupported models should be marked as Inconclusive** — Instead of silently passing with a warning, use `Assert.Inconclusive()` (or equivalent) to clearly signal that the model was skipped, not verified.
3. **Summary assertion** — Consider adding a final test or test fixture teardown that verifies at least one model passed the strict tool-calling assertions.

## Files to Modify

- `src/Cisharpai.Integration.Tests/AzureAiInference/AzureAiInferenceToolCallingIntegrationTests.cs`

## Reference

- Other provider tool-calling tests that do strict assertions: `src/Cisharpai.Integration.Tests/OpenAi/OpenAiToolCallingIntegrationTests.cs`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unsupported models produce Inconclusive test results, not green passes
- If zero models support tool calling, the overall test result is not all-green
- At least one configured model must pass strict tool-calling assertions for tests to be considered passing

description:
## Summary
Add a new `PostStreamAsync` method to `LlmHttpClient` that handles Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming. This method yields raw JSON strings from SSE `data:` lines.

## Files to Modify
**`src/Cisharpai/LlmHttpClient.cs`**

## Implementation Details

Add a new method alongside existing `PostAsync` and `PostWithRawAsync`:

```csharp
public async IAsyncEnumerable<string> PostStreamAsync<TRequest>(
    string uri,
    TRequest payload,
    [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken cancellationToken = default,
    JsonElement? extraParameters = null)
```

### Method Logic

1. **Serialize the request** using the existing `SerializeAndMerge` private method (reuse existing logic for extra parameters deep merge).

2. **Send the HTTP request** with `HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead`:
   ```csharp
   var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, uri)
   {
       Content = new StringContent(json, Encoding.UTF8, "application/json")
   };
   var response = await _httpClient.SendAsync(request, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead, cancellationToken);
   ```

3. **Check status code** — on non-2xx, throw `LlmHttpRequestException` (same pattern as existing methods). This happens before any chunks are yielded, so the caller gets the exception immediately.

4. **Read the response body line-by-line**:
   ```csharp
   using var stream = await response.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(cancellationToken);
   using var reader = new StreamReader(stream);
   
   while (!reader.EndOfStream)
   {
       cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();
       var line = await reader.ReadLineAsync(cancellationToken);
       
       if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(line)) continue;        // blank lines between events
       if (line.StartsWith("event:")) continue;          // named event lines (Anthropic/Cohere)
       if (line == "data: [DONE]") yield break;          // OpenAI/Azure convention
       if (!line.StartsWith("data: ")) continue;         // skip non-data lines
       
       var json = line.Substring(6);                      // strip "data: " prefix
       yield return json;
   }
   ```

5. **Resource disposal** — The `HttpRequestMessage`, `HttpResponseMessage`, stream, and reader must NOT be disposed until the enumerable is fully consumed. Use `try/finally` blocks:
   ```csharp
   HttpResponseMessage? response = null;
   try
   {
       // ... send request, check status, yield lines ...
   }
   finally
   {
       response?.Dispose();
   }
   ```

### SSE Format Reference
All providers use the SSE format with slight variations:
- **OpenAI/Azure**: `data: {...}\n\n` terminated by `data: [DONE]`
- **Anthropic**: `event: content_block_delta\ndata: {...}\n\n` (no `[DONE]`, stream just ends)
- **Cohere**: `event: content-delta\ndata: {...}\n\n` (no `[DONE]`, stream just ends)

The method handles all of these by:
- Ignoring `event:` lines (provider clients use the `type` field inside the JSON data)
- Stopping on `data: [DONE]` (OpenAI)
- Naturally completing when the stream ends (Anthropic/Cohere)

### Important Notes
- Add `using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;` for `[EnumeratorCancellation]`
- The method yields raw JSON strings — each provider is responsible for deserializing into its own delta DTO
- `ReadLineAsync` on .NET 8+ accepts `CancellationToken` — use the overload
- Ensure the `HttpResponseMessage` is disposed in the finally block even if the caller breaks out early

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `PostStreamAsync` method added to `LlmHttpClient`
- [ ] Handles SSE `data:` prefix stripping
- [ ] Handles `data: [DONE]` termination
- [ ] Handles blank lines and `event:` lines
- [ ] Proper resource disposal with try/finally
- [ ] Non-2xx responses throw `LlmHttpRequestException`
- [ ] Project builds successfully
